items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: He’d say, “hey I don’t want to talk about them, I want to talk about the band I have now.”

ctx.x: Wow. It almost sounds like the story I’ve heard about when Charlie Christian was introduced on the bandstand that particular night and he just was inspired to play even beyond himself.

Yeah. But that’s the thing. You know if you’re going to play music, if you’ve made this commitment, the worst thing you can do for yourself is treat it like a job and show up — © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

like these kind of things — we’re on a jazz party right now. It’s very easy to just go and play the same old tunes. And a lot of people do, to be honest, and get very lazy about it. But it’s not worth my while personally to get up there and just go through the motions. Even if I’m playing somebody else’s same old tune, I’m trying to play some music, for good or for bad. I’m not saying I’m a great musician but at least I try. Otherwise there’s no point to playing music. You could be doing something else and making…
